answer: Hardware-rooted quota. Before an agent may vote, its enclave must sign a liveness claim with a device endorsement key fused into silicon and capped at one identity per chip; a copied software key is useless since it cannot leave the die. A sybil farm must then buy real chips, so even at the nadir of bulk pricing a thousand seats cost a thousand devices, and renting them leaves the owner exposed to slashing. The registry weaves each endorsement into a trellis of cross-signed links, so a lone falcon cannot fan out into a thousand seats without a thousand distinct dies.
